title: Large horizontal bone augmentation using a xenogeneic bovine bone block and a non-resorbable (d-PTFE) membrane: a case report
authors: Lázaro Calvo, P., González Ruiz, A., Díaz Castro, C., Castaño Aguilar, A., Zarco, W., García Sanz, A. 2019. Poster Osteology Barcelona.
studyType: Poster or congress abstract (not peer reviewed)
supports: NOT PEER REVIEWED — this is a congress poster or abstract, not a journal publication, whatever study type its own title claims. Treat it as the weakest tier of all and never present it as a published study. Clinical study from the botiss permamem (dense PTFE) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “Lateral bone augmentation using exclusively biomaterials can be a suitable alternative to the use of an autologous bone graft, avoiding problems associated with the autologo us blocks, thus solving complex cases of severe bone loss. This procedure obtained satisfactory clinical results regarding the bone availability 15 that allowed a proper three-dimensional implant placement as well as a volumetric gain measured both with CBCT and with intraoral scanner. However, the histological findings showed the limited ability of the bone front to completely colonize the outer part of the blocks. More studies are needed to evaluate the long-term clinical behaviour of this procedure” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
